training.stop_reason: frozen early-stop rule: 40 consecutive complete epochs without a strict new validation high
training.lr_schedule_never_decayed: MultiStepLR milestones [120,180] were never reached because the run stopped at epoch 64

independent_validation_108.protocol: strict reload of the trainer-selected checkpoint only; no per-epoch evaluation, no re-selection

comparisons.note: Descriptive context only. This arm is NOT a controlled contrast: full unfreeze, inverted LR direction, N4, epochs, batch and multi-GPU all changed together.

each_model_on_its_own_training_preproces.why: each model evaluated under the preprocessing it was trained on, i.e. each at its own best

both_on_n4_inputs.why: Equalizes evaluation inputs but handicaps LoRA, which was trained without N4 and therefore suffers a train/eval mismatch here. This OVERSTATES the difference.

comparisons.no_paired_bootstrap: Deliberately not computed. The arms differ in training preprocessing, so a paired confidence interval would imply an inferential rigour the design does not support.

target_gap.caveat: 0.741 was measured by DPD-SAM's authors on their own split under an undisclosed prompt protocol. It is not a like-for-like target and reaching it here would not constitute reproduction.

lessons_for_next_arm: patience (40) must exceed the largest LR milestone (120) or the decay schedule is unreachable; this run stopped at epoch 64 and never decayed
overfitting appeared early: train-val gap grew from -0.05 (epoch 1) to +0.13 (epoch 35) while val plateaued near 0.55
best validation arrived at epoch 24 of a 200-epoch budget, so the epoch budget was not the binding constraint
equalizing evaluation preprocessing across arms is not automatically fairer; it can transfer the mismatch penalty to the other arm
